memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "And the Lord has declared this day that you are his people, his treasured possession as he promised, and that you are to keep all his commands. He has declared that he will set you in praise, fame and honour high above all the nations he has made and that you will be a people holy to the Lord your God, as he promised." — Deut 26:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
What a stunning declaration to close the chapter. The people had declared the Lord as their God — and now God declares them as His people, His "treasured possession." Out of all the nations, He set His love on Israel, not because they were greater, but simply because He chose to love them. They were precious to Him.

Pause on that phrase: treasured possession. The God who owns the whole universe looked at this small, freed-slave nation and called them His treasure. That is not because of anything in them. It is because of the kind of God He is — a God who loves and cherishes His own.

If you belong to Christ, the New Testament lifts this very language and places it on you. Peter tells believers we are "a chosen people... God's special possession" (1 Pet 2:9). Through Jesus, we are gathered into the people God treasures. You are not tolerated by God; you are treasured by Him.

And with this belonging comes a calling — to be holy, set apart for Him. Being God's treasured people is meant to shape how we live, marking us out as different for His glory. We are cherished by grace, and called to holiness in response. What love, that the Holy God should call us His own treasure.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I really believe that God treasures me?
2. How would living as God's "treasured possession" change my day?
3. What does being "holy to the Lord" call me to leave behind?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, it amazes me that You would call me Your treasured possession. Thank You for choosing to love me in Christ. Help me live as Your holy people, set apart for Your glory. Amen.
